title: Simulate fixed native-continuous and stepped trailing stop execution
description:
Implement shadow protective-stop simulation in mike_trade/brokers/shadow/stops.py. It must use the same provider-neutral protection policies that production uses, with no duplicated policy math. It simulates three types:
- fixed stops
- native-continuous-equivalent trailing stops: a high-water mark tracked from eligible quotes, with the stop at high-water minus trail amount/percent
- stepped trailing stops: the stop ratchets in configured steps after configured gains

Rules:
- Protection begins only after a confirmed positive shadow fill.
- It always covers the actual remaining position quantity, including after partial fills.
- For a long position the stop price never moves downward.
- Stop trigger evaluation uses an explicit, configurable trigger assumption (for example bid <= stop, or last trade <= stop where available).
- Triggered stop execution uses the bid plus configured stop slippage. The resulting sell is executed through the p.1 account/ledger so the sell quantity never exceeds the held quantity.
- Coordinate with discretionary/manual exits. When an ordinary exit is pending or filled, the protective stop is cancelled or reduced so that overlapping sells cannot create a short position.
- Gaps through the stop fill at the available bid, not at the stop price.
- Missing or stale quotes leave the stop state as UNKNOWN/unevaluated with a reason. They do not produce fabricated triggers.
- Every stop state change and trigger is recorded with simulator version, assumptions and feed provenance, and is labeled estimated and not broker-confirmed.
- Stop state must be restorable from the ledger on restart.

All prices and quantities are Decimal, and times are UTC-aware.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/brokers/shadow/account.py and mike_trade/brokers/shadow/ledger.py (from p.1)
- the existing provider-neutral protective/trailing stop policy module(s) and stop state types under mike_trade/ from earlier phases
- existing quote/market-snapshot types and the exit coordination/order-intent types

Write tests/unit/test_shadow_stops.py covering both positive and negative cases.
acceptance_criteria: A fixed stop triggers when the configured trigger condition is met and sells the full remaining quantity at bid minus configured slippage (exact Decimal assertion)
The continuous trailing stop tracks the high-water mark and the stop price never decreases for a long position across a rising-then-falling quote sequence
The stepped trailing stop ratchets only at configured step thresholds and never moves downward
No stop is armed before a confirmed positive fill; after a partial fill the stop covers exactly the filled remaining quantity
A gap below the stop fills at the available bid, not at the stop price
When a discretionary exit fills first, the protective stop is cancelled/reduced and the total sold never exceeds the held quantity (no short position)
Missing or stale quotes leave the stop evaluation UNKNOWN with a recorded reason and produce no trigger
The policy computation calls the shared production provider-neutral policy functions rather than reimplementing separate stop math
Stop state/trigger records include simulator version, assumptions, provenance, estimated=True and broker_confirmed=False, and are restored identically from the ledger
The module imports no Alpaca trading client or broker credential configuration
tests/unit/test_shadow_stops.py exists with positive and negative tests and passes when run alone
forbidden_changes: modify files outside allowed_write_paths, including shared production stop policy modules and mike_trade/brokers/shadow/account.py, ledger.py, fills.py
change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
move a long stop price downward
fabricate stop triggers or fill prices without quote evidence
import or call any Alpaca trading client, paper/live endpoint, or broker credential
use float for prices or quantities
create live broker orders or run broad test suites/backtests
